description: Differentiates a composite function as a sum of the parts' derivatives instead of their product.
manifestation: Given f(g(x)), computes f'(x) + g'(x) instead of f'(g(x)) * g'(x); in a network, this shows up as adding rather than multiplying layer-local gradients.

description: Believes each layer's weight update uses only that layer's local error, ignoring gradients flowing back from downstream layers.
manifestation: Updates a hidden layer as if it were the output layer, skipping the upstream chain of partial derivatives entirely.

description: Believes a plateauing training loss always means the model has converged optimally, rather than considering vanishing/exploding gradients.
manifestation: Stops debugging a stalled training run because 'the loss curve is flat', without checking gradient magnitudes or learning rate.

description: Believes overfitting can only happen with very small datasets and cannot happen once there is 'enough' data.
manifestation: Dismisses a large train/validation gap as impossible given dataset size, rather than checking model capacity vs. data complexity.

description: Believes running cross-validation itself prevents overfitting, rather than merely detecting/estimating it.
manifestation: Adds k-fold CV to a pipeline and assumes the resulting model is now regularized, with no other changes made.

description: Believes ReLU has no drawbacks and should replace sigmoid/softmax everywhere, including output layers for probabilities.
manifestation: Uses ReLU on a final classification layer where a bounded probability output (softmax/sigmoid) is required.

description: Believes stochastic gradient descent and full-batch gradient descent always follow the same trajectory, ignoring sampling noise.
manifestation: Expects a single-example SGD step to reduce loss on the whole training set every step, the way a full-batch step would.

description: Believes INNER JOIN keeps all rows from both tables, similar to a UNION.
manifestation: Expects unmatched rows from either table to appear (with NULLs) in an INNER JOIN result, then is surprised rows are missing.

description: Believes LEFT JOIN and RIGHT JOIN with the tables in the same order return the same rows, missing that row-preservation direction matters.
manifestation: Swaps LEFT JOIN for RIGHT JOIN (same table order) expecting identical output.

description: Believes a p-value is the probability that the null hypothesis is true.
manifestation: States 'p = 0.03 means there's a 3% chance the null hypothesis is true', a direct misreading of what a p-value conditions on.

description: Believes a 95% confidence interval means there's a 95% chance the true parameter lies in this specific computed interval.
manifestation: Interprets one already-computed 95% CI as having a 95% chance of containing the true population parameter, rather than describing the procedure's long-run coverage.

description: Believes a recursive function will naturally terminate as long as the input 'gets smaller', without an explicit base case.
manifestation: Writes a recursive function with only a recursive call and no explicit stopping condition, causing infinite recursion / stack overflow.

description: Conflates Big-O with worst-case runtime specifically, not realizing O/Θ/Ω describe upper/tight/lower bounds independent of best/average/worst case.
manifestation: States an algorithm 'is O(n log n)' meaning strictly worst-case, then is confused when a source describes its average-case bound the same way.

description: Believes it's acceptable to perform state-mutating writes inside a GET endpoint since 'it still works'.
manifestation: Implements a GET /delete-item endpoint, breaking caching, prefetching and idempotency assumptions that depend on GET being safe.

description: Believes a JWT's payload is encrypted and therefore safe to store secrets in, when it is only signed and base64-encoded (readable by anyone).
manifestation: Puts a plaintext secret or password inside a JWT claim, assuming it can't be read by the client that holds the token.

description: Believes a fully passing unit test suite proves the absence of bugs, rather than only the absence of the specific behaviors tested.
manifestation: Ships a change on 'all tests green' without considering untested edge cases or integration behavior.

description: Conflates a Docker image with a running container, believing stopping a container deletes its image.
manifestation: Runs `docker stop` and then expects `docker run` on the same image to fail because 'the container/image is gone'.

description: Believes fully normalizing a relational schema (3NF and beyond) always improves query performance.
manifestation: Over-normalizes a reporting table into many joins, then is surprised query latency gets worse, not better.
